summary: Wrote a 25-test Playwright/Chromium suite under tests/01-for-index-html-page-in-idee/ (registered in playwright.config.js testMatch) driving the real index.html with a fake mic and a stubbed webkitSpeechRecognition/SpeechRecognition. It covers all 8 numbered acceptance checks (no language/prompt multipart part from either #btn-idea-dictate or #btn-dictate, exact untranslated round-trip in both languages, the English-only model swap for groq/openai/custom, tidy-up accepting a punctuation fix and rejecting a translation, the chat system prompt never mentioning 'missing Romanian diacritics', and the live engine still using ro-RO/en-US) plus edge cases on pickModel()'s regex (bare 'en', case-insensitive '.en' suffix, ids that merely contain 'en', empty saved model) and keepsWords()'s two thresholds (exact 80%/0.8x boundary, just-below rejection, padding past 1.25x, token-collapsing under 0.8x) and tidy-up's HTTP-error/empty-reply fallbacks. All 25 tests pass against the implementer's js/markdown/dictation.js. The existing dictate/idea/nav Node suites and node tests/verify.js were re-run and show the same baseline results as main (idea's and nav's pre-existing known failures only), so no regression. No product bugs were found; the only defects found during authoring were in the test suite itself (a too-short fake-mic recording window, and stubbing only webkitSpeechRecognition while Chrome also exposes an unprefixed SpeechRecognition that dictation.js tries first) and were fixed before this report.
